pinned_source.title: On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling
pinned_source.reading_method: Raw pinned HTML, rendered locally by preserving MathML alttext and selecting only assigned sections plus their own stated lemmas. No existing source restatement, topology, target, or audit was used.

bounded_anchors_read.purpose: Admissible class; Eq. (1); Borel randomized query/stopping/output model; Eq. (2); deterministic cap and seed-averaged law.
Actual Eq. (11) cosine spectrum and full Haar orthogonal rotation, spectrum publicity and seed independence.
B.1 primitive-query reduction, legal histories, absorbing stopping, transcript kernels and common seed integration.
C.1 finite query horizon, seed, dummy zero queries, latent analysis histories and law-preserving auxiliary extension.
C.4 ordinary quadratic, spectral admissibility, Hessian, unique minimizer and Gaussian normalization.
Own statement of Lemma 4.3, exact 2q+1<d condition, Krylov definition, output vector and coefficient scope needed to interpret C.1.
Own statement of Lemma 4.6: admissibility for every O in O(d).

pinned_source.retained_source_expression: Only formulas necessary for this conditions receipt; no full source or section copies retained.

objects.meaning: A is a real symmetric precision matrix. f_A(x)=x^T A x/2, pi_A=N(0,A^{-1}), and FO_A(x)=(x^T A x/2, A x). A randomized algorithm has private randomness, adaptive oracle queries, Borel stopping decisions and an R^d-valued Borel output. rho_A^Alg is its entire output law, including all private randomness.

domains.meaning: General preliminaries use integer d>=1, kappa>=1, x in R^d, and A in A_{d,kappa}={A=A^T: I_d<=A<=kappa I_d} in Loewner order. The Section 4 hard family instead has d>=2 and kappa>=2. Eq. (11) uses i=1,...,d, theta_i=(i-1/2)pi/d, lambda_i=(kappa+1)/2+(kappa-1)cos(theta_i)/2 and Lambda=diag(lambda_1,...,lambda_d). O ranges over the full real orthogonal group O(d), not a diagonal or coordinatewise family.

quantifiers.meaning: An algorithm is one causal collection of Borel rules using its seed and previous answers. A fixed query budget T means at most T actual queries for every admissible input and every seed realization. For 0<epsilon<1, Q_G is the infimum over nonnegative integer caps T for which there exists such an algorithm with sup_A TV(rho_A^Alg,pi_A)<=epsilon. Lemma 4.6 admits every orthogonal O. The hard-family experiment draws O Haar independently of the algorithm's private randomness.

assumptions.meaning: The input randomness and algorithm randomness are independent. Query choice, stopping and output are Borel functions of the allowed information. The cap is deterministic and pathwise. A positive definite quadratic in the prescribed spectral class supplies an invertible precision and Gaussian target. Section 4 permits public knowledge of its fixed deterministic spectrum; the unknown part is the eigenbasis. No query-span restriction, linearity of the policy, seedwise accuracy or expected-query budget is imposed in Section 2.

conclusion.meaning: Eq. (1) is literal exact value-and-gradient oracle access. Exact matrix-vector, gradient-only and value-and-gradient access have the same query complexity on this class, because A x is returned and x^T A x/2 is recoverable from x and A x. Eq. (2) concerns uniform total-variation approximation by the seed-averaged output law. The fixed spectrum does not make its rotated precision known. C.4 proves admissibility of the ordinary quadratic for the actual full orthogonal family.

scopes_and_senses.meaning: All oracle arithmetic is exact. The gradient A x and quadratic x^T A x use the full matrix in the original coordinates, with the cross terms of a rotated matrix. In the fixed-family analysis A=O Lambda O^T; hidden coordinates u=O^T x are analysis variables, not oracle output. Borel adaptivity and arbitrary Borel output remain in force. The source averages the law over the seed and takes a supremum over inputs; these are different operations. The norm is Euclidean, and matrix inequalities are Loewner inequalities.

constant_dependencies.meaning: T is a nonnegative integer cap; Q_G depends on d,kappa,epsilon with 0<epsilon<1. Lambda depends on d and kappa but not on O or the seed. The normalizer Z_A=(2pi)^{d/2}(det Lambda)^{-1/2} is therefore independent of O and public with the spectrum. The finite-history arguments have their own conditions: B.1 uses 2T<n and k blocks, hence padded primitive horizon M=2Tk; Lemma 4.3 states integer q>=0 and 2q+1<d. These contextual thresholds are not added as global restrictions to the Section 2 oracle definition.

B1_absorbing_and_common_seed: B.1 concerns independent determinant-conditioned orthogonal blocks O_j with common determinant sign b; its primitive oracle can ask O_j v or O_j^T v. This is a separate source construction from Section 4's single full Haar eigenbasis.
One first-order query is simulated by at most two primitive queries per block. The strict 2T<n bound ensures at least two unexposed dimensions before a nonterminal fresh observation.

After stopping, the history receives an absorbing symbol and all states remain unchanged. At terminal histories the next action is dagger and its response law is delta_dagger. The padded transcript has a deterministic horizon M=2Tk.

The sign-independent response kernel may be extended arbitrarily outside legal histories. That extension is a proof kernel convention, not permission to change the literal exact oracle on actual legal queries.

For each fixed complete seed xi, the primitive simulation is deterministic. Transcript indistinguishability is proved first, then integrated over the same seed law under both signs. The resulting equality is a joint-law equality for (xi,H_M), and the Borel output Psi(xi,H_M) preserves it.
C1_finite_horizon_and_information: The stated Lemma 4.3 has q>=0 and 2q+1<d. The proof pads an at-most-q algorithm with zero queries to exactly q queries; this preserves the original output experiment.
R is independent of O. The next x_i is measurable in R and previous gradient replies. The scalar reply adds no information beyond the query and the gradient reply.
The final output is treated as x_{q+1}=X for one extra preimage revelation, without an extra charged oracle query or extra oracle reply.

The extended probability space adds independent Z_1,...,Z_{q+1} standard Gaussian vectors and preserves the joint law of O,R,transcript,X. Its enlarged histories contain latent u_i=O^T x_i; these histories are analysis devices, not information supplied to the algorithm.

The Haar state records measurable E and OP_E and the conditional Haar law on the complementary isometry. Zero unexplored components reveal nothing and are handled separately, rather than assigned a fictitious uniform direction.

The constructed g_i are mutually independent standard Gaussians with nonrandom conditional law given the prior enlarged history. The source does not assert that these constructed g_i are independent of O or X. Polynomial coefficients in the final span representation may depend on the entire extended experiment.
The finite span conclusion is almost sure: O^T X belongs to span{Lambda^j g_a:1<=a<=q+1,0<=j<=q}. It does not impose an a priori Krylov or query-response-span restriction on the algorithm.
C4_ordinary_quadratic: For Eq. (11)'s range, 0<theta_i<pi and 1<lambda_i<kappa. Orthogonal conjugation gives I_d<=A<=kappa I_d for every orthogonal O.
V_A(x)=x^T A x/2 has constant Hessian A, is C-infinity, 1-strongly convex and kappa-smooth, and has unique minimizer 0 because V_A(0)=0 and V_A(x)>=||x||^2/2>0 for x!=0.
The target and normalizer are those of the full ordinary quadratic; the determinant is invariant under O Lambda O^T.

definition_and_model_hazards_to_check_on.hazard: Replacing A x with coordinatewise diagonal multiplication or replacing x^T A x with only diagonal entries changes the rotated family. The general exact oracle must retain the full matrix action.

A fixed deterministic Lambda is the spectrum; the actual public family is O Lambda O^T for all O in O(d), with Haar used for the hard-input experiment. Restricting O to identity, signed permutations, diagonal matrices, or one determinant component requires a separate justification.
The whole seed law is common and input independent. A model that samples the seed from a law depending on the input can leak the unknown matrix even when its query functions look causal.

Queries, stop decisions and output must use the seed and prior replies. An interface with a direct unknown A or O argument in the decision rule needs an explicit information restriction; merely calling the rule adaptive would not supply one.
A deterministic cap for every input and seed realization differs from an expected cap or almost-sure-only bound. Accuracy is seed averaged, not asserted seed by seed.

Finite padded execution must preserve stopping and the output chosen at stopping. Continuing genuine information-bearing queries after a stop and then using their responses would change the experiment.

The source does not prescribe a specific seed carrier or uniform seed distribution. Any such representation must account for the same Borel randomized law rather than silently narrow the source algorithm class.

Source oracle/potential/target definitions have ordinary mathematical meanings on their stated carriers. An if/default/fallback that changes their values on admitted matrices or legal histories would be substantive. Arbitrary proof-kernel extension outside legal histories in B.1 has a different scope.

Auxiliary Gaussian vectors and hidden-coordinate revelations in C.1 belong to the enlarged analysis probability space. They must not become free algorithmic input, a new charged query, or a hypothesis that the output already lies in a Krylov span.
The B.1 sign-conditioned block dimensions n,k,2T<n and the C.1 full-Haar eigenbasis dimensions d,q,2q+1<d must remain separate; neither proof context redefines Section 2's general oracle class.

The seed-averaged law, Haar-average law and uniform-in-input TV bound are distinct measures or quantifier scopes. An equality or bound after one averaging operation does not by itself establish the others.

Orthogonal representations of a fixed precision need not be unique, but the ordinary potential, exact oracle and target are functions of A. Latent-coordinate claims may additionally refer to the chosen O and must be interpreted in that joint experiment.
